authored.objective: sv2-syntax parses a lossless CST against TWO grammars, chosen by file suffix: KerML and SysML have two start symbols, and sv2_syntax::parse requires a Language with no default (ADR-0014, implemented 2026-09-18). It reads packages, imports, aliases, annotating elements as members in both grammars, KerML's eight classifiers, SysML's eight definitions, seven usages with all five feature specializations, and the expression operator core: 124 of 558 productions. Diagnostics are typed: Parse::errors() returns Diagnostic, each carrying a TextRange, a namespaced code and a severity, and OffsetMap is the single designated offset boundary. The reference grammar is DERIVED IN FULL through the six-phase pipeline and FROZEN at sha256 0b9abe64f1f3ce2b: 554 of 554 live units verified, none pending and none in conflict, in both languages. The derived grammar's oracle parses every one of the 311 corpus files and catches all 37 negatives, leaking none. The RUST parser is far behind that oracle and the gap is measured rather than assumed: it accepts 26 of 253 .sysml and 2 of 58 .kerml corpus files, recorded per file in tests/corpus-accepted.txt and ratcheted by scripts/corpus_sweep.py. That set may grow and must never shrink.
authored.next_step:
THE PARSER AGAIN, in measured order. Re-measure before starting: parse every failing corpus file and count the token its FIRST diagnostic names. The ordering has changed every time productions landed, and these numbers are from 2026-09-18.
KerML, 56 failing: feature 33, then a tail of twos and ones.
SysML, 227 failing: action 36, port 15, requirement 13, perform 10, metadata 9, ref 9, constraint 9, ':>>' 8, '[' 8, calc 7.

(1) PortDefinition is the cheapest win at 15 files. It is already on the definition spine and needs only ConjugatedPortDefinitionMember, the one part that kept it out of SIMPLE_DEFINITIONS. tests/rejection/port-definition-is-not-implemented.sysml says exactly that and is the case to remove when it lands.
(2) KERML'S Feature (8.2.4.3.1) -- 33 of 56 failing KerML files, and essentially the whole remaining KerML gap. NamespaceFeatureMember -> FeatureElement -> Feature, and FeatureDeclaration carries the specialization parts. tests/rejection/end-feature-requires-a-declaration.kerml already states one rule about it.
(3) ActionBody is the largest SysML item at 36 files and a bigger piece of work than any table so far, because it is a BODY rather than a declaration -- action nodes and successions. calc, constraint, requirement and state each want a specialised body too; check whether any of those bodies share a shape the way the classifiers and the definitions did, BEFORE writing any of them.

METHOD THAT KEEPS WORKING: derive the table, do not choose it. Both tables so far came from matching rule shapes across the verified units in .claude/state/grammar/units -- eleven productions share `TypePrefix KW Decl Body` and exactly eight share the classifier spine; twenty-two contain a `def` and exactly eight end in Definition. Reading the clause prose and typing a list would have included action and port, both of which would have been wrong. Every element needs its coverage marker, a positive case, and a rejection case in the same change, and `scripts/corpus-sweep.sh --record` moves the ledger, upward only.

DIAGNOSTICS ARE DONE and the shape is settled; follow it. A new diagnostic gets a DiagnosticCode variant with a PARSE- wire name and a severity on the code, and it is raised through Parser::emit with a range from Parser::here or Parser::range_of. Do not add a String error anywhere; Diagnostic cannot be built without a range, which is the point. Do not merge DiagnosticCode with sv2-cli's ErrorCode -- that one is about the PROCESS and maps onto exit statuses (STD-002-RS §3.2).

THE BLOCKING DECISION, unchanged and now the oldest thing outstanding: element identity. ADR-0009 and ADR-0016 both decide it, both are `proposed`, and neither carries supersedes/superseded-by frontmatter naming the other. It blocks the sidecar schema, stable handles in sv2-resolve, and any bidirectional graphical edit -- which is the whole point of the end state. Nothing above this line unblocks it, and it gets no cheaper by waiting.

TWO KNOWN GAPS, deliberate:
(a) A bare `/* ... */` at member position is Comment's shortest form by 8.2.2.4.2 and this parser still attaches it as trivia. Both readings keep every byte so the round trip holds, but the tree shape differs from the specification's. Switching it changes every tree that has a comment in it and wants its own snapshot review. See Parser::at_annotating_member.
(b) OffsetMap has line_col and no UTF-8/UTF-16 conversion. That is not an oversight: ADR-0013 is still `proposed` and neither sv2-lsp nor sv2-wasm exists. When one does, the conversion goes in offset.rs and nowhere else (Seam 3, RISK-013-2, FIT-5).

RESOLVED as far as it can be on one machine. The wikis are pinned by receipt: 1651 atoms in .claude/state/wiki-receipts.json, each with its clause, page, the wiki's region_sha256 to the source PDF span, and a file hash. Drift now fails the gate, and a citation naming a receipt that was never pinned now fails scripts/check_citations.py. NOT resolved: the wikis are not in the repository, because their 1651 atoms carry ~2.3 MB of verbatim OMG specification prose with no licence notice, and this repository is MIT and public. Revisit only if OMG's licensing changes, or if the wiki builder can be pinned and rerun from locally-held PDFs as part of a bootstrap.

pending_decisions.question: RESOLVED. regen_state.py recorded `git log --oneline -8` in the generated block and --check compared it, which has no fixed point: the commit carrying state.json cannot record its own hash, and amending only moves it. The gate was therefore red after every commit, for ever. Fixed by naming the compared measurements explicitly — COMPARED = (coverage, tests, pins) — and a pure is_stale() over them, with four tests including the one that says a new commit is not staleness. `commits` is still measured and written for whoever reads the block at session start; it is simply not evidence. Nothing else read it: not state_report.py, not the schema's required list. NOT weakened: coverage, tests and pins are still compared exactly as before, so an un-regenerated block after real work still fails.

RESOLVED: the derive-grammar six-phase pipeline. It runs, and the expression layer is being derived through it starting from KerML 8.2.5.8.1. Two pipeline defects had to be fixed first (plan enumerated the Xtext inventory; freeze check went red on the first derived unit); both are fixed and tested.

RESOLVED. A unit no longer embeds its clause: it keeps the citation and a sha256 of the clause text, and grammar_next.py joins the text from the local export at read time. The units are therefore committed, so the derived rules, decisions and evidence survive a clone and are reviewable in a diff, while no specification prose enters the repository. check_derivation_text.py holds the line on every gate. NOT resolved by this: a fresh clone still cannot re-derive or verify a clause without building the wikis from locally-held PDFs, which is the standing wiki-reproducibility limit.

How is '[' disambiguated between MultiplicityPart and BracketExpression? Both are implemented-or-planned in the same grammar and the token is identical. The working hypothesis is positional -- a '[' reached from UsageDeclaration's FeatureSpecializationPart is a multiplicity, a '[' reached from an expression operand is a BracketExpression -- which is what the current code already does by construction, since multiplicity_part is only called from feature_specialization_part. Confirm that holds for every corpus shape before BracketExpression lands, in particular where a value part's expression is followed by a unit: `attribute m = 1200 [kg];` reaches the '[' from the expression side with a MultiplicityPart already consumed on the declaration side.
blocks: BracketExpression, IndexExpression, and the 297 corpus files that write a bracketed unit

pending_decisions.question: Is MAX_DEPTH = 400 in crates/sv2-syntax/src/parser.rs the right recursion limit, and should it be configurable? It was introduced this session because the recursive expression parser OVERFLOWED THE STACK, which aborts the process and so is strictly worse than the panic invariant 3 forbids. Measured thresholds before the guard: unary operators between 2000 and 5000 levels, parenthesised expressions and nested bodies between 5000 and 10000. Note the nested-body path had this flaw ALREADY -- it is not new with the expression layer. 400 is far past anything a person writes, but it is a number nobody derived from a source, and it changes what the parser accepts.

log.summary: Closed the SysML grammar and froze the reference. 473 to 554 of 554 live units verified, none pending and none in conflict; frozen at sha256 0b9abe64f1f3ce2b, 554 productions, ledger entry 1. The oracle went from 155 to all 311 corpus files accepted, still catching all 37 negatives with none leaked. Four filed specification defects repaired and recorded, each issue page fetched and read: SYSML21-408 and -624 (both in SendNode's single line), -400 (ControlNodePrefix) and -401 (TriggerExpression). ForVariableDeclarationMember adjudicated, which left SysML with no unreachable production. The oracle's state guard was re-derived from a measurement: ~143 items per token scaling linearly, so the 400_000 absolute cap was mis-calibrated rather than the grammar ambiguous, and it is now a per-token budget with four tests. Also declared sv2-ast, sv2-hir and sv2-resolve as stub crates, and proposed ADR-0016 and ADR-0017.

Implemented the expression operator core: OwnedExpression by precedence climbing over the fifteen tiers of KerML 8.2.5.8.1 table 6, plus MultiplicityPart, ValuePart and ElementFilterMember, which it unblocked. Coverage 57 to 106 of 558; negative cases 49 to 65. Precedence is NOT in the grammar and cannot be -- note 2 of that clause says so -- so the parser reads docs/operator-precedence.toml, and a test diffs that file against the parser's INFIX table both ways so neither can be edited alone; deviations.json had already recorded the decision under BinaryOperatorExpression as spec_only/follow_spec. Found and fixed a defect this introduced: deep nesting overflowed the stack, which aborts rather than panics and so breaks invariant 3; added MAX_DEPTH and a round-trip test at 50000 levels for parentheses, unary operators and nested bodies. spec-conformance-reviewer returned one blocking finding, all fixed: the FeatureSpecializationPart comment quoted the Pilot's '( -> FeatureSpecialization )+' syntactic predicate as though it were KerML 8.2.4.3.1, and that '->' is in neither specification's BNF. Also committed a draft docs/CRATES.md and the author's spelling corrections to README.md and NOTICE.md.
